title: Service function chain deployment method based on federal reinforcement learning
assignee: Beijing Beishang Xidian Technology Co ltd

pse.problem: Existing service function chain (SFC) deployment technologies are not applicable to the complex and changeable IoT network, causing solution delay, local optimum traps, or slow convergence due to exploration of the huge IoT network space.
pse.solution_function: The method performs joint optimization of SFC deployment cost and energy consumption in a cloud-edge collaborative network scenario. It establishes two local SFC deployment algorithms based on parameterized deep Q-learning (P-DQN) for latency-sensitive and resource-intensive IoT network application requests at different time scales. A global SFC deployment model is trained using these parameters via federated learning, with a window value-based asynchronous federation.
pse.solution_structure: The system consists of cloud servers, edge servers, service function chains (SFC), and a federated learning framework. The federated learning framework coordinates the local P-DQN algorithms on each edge server and the global SFC deployment model.
pse.solution_implementation: In the cloud-edge collaborative network, the system deploys SFC at both the edge and the cloud to jointly optimize cost and energy consumption. At the edge level, two local P-DQN algorithms are employed for latency-sensitive and resource-intensive requests. The learned parameters from these algorithms are shared and used to train a global SFC deployment model via federated learning, which implements asynchronous updates based on a window value.
pse.effect: The method improves the efficiency of SFC deployment in IoT networks by addressing solution delay, local optimum traps, and slow convergence issues through the use of parameterized deep Q-learning and federated learning.
